A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SafeKey study. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety and general-capability evaluations, method ablations, reasoning analyses and an appendix human-annotation study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds RL/DPO comparisons, training–test similarity measurements and an expanded reasoning-pattern analysis.

M1.justification: SafeKey's Dual-Path Safety Head, Query-Mask Modeling, combined training objective and inference procedure remain unchanged in Section 3. The newly evaluated RL and DPO approaches are baselines, not modifications to SafeKey.

E1.justification: The STAR-1 training coverage and existing safety, jailbreak, over-refusal and general-capability evaluation tasks are retained. The added analyses reuse these datasets; additional model configurations and comparison methods do not introduce new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: v1's principal comparison includes R1 Distilled and SFT. v2 adds GRPO-based RL and DPO baselines across 7B, 8B and 14B models in Appendix A.4 and Table 4, substantially broadening the evaluated alignment approaches.

E3.justification: v2 introduces distinct baseline-training protocols: two GRPO epochs with format and final-answer safety rewards, and DPO using generated negative responses with SFT-matched epoch counts. It also introduces similarity and prompt-length measurements and extends Section 2.1's annotation study to 14B variants, sampling 30 responses per model. Existing main evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.3 examines separation between training and test distributions using embedding similarity, prompt lengths and prefilling status. Section 2.1 extends the reasoning-pattern check to 14B models. Existing component ablations, attention and representation analyses, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Parenthesized values in Table 2 remain harmfulness scores, not uncertainty estimates; the new results do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–7 retain their results. New Table 4 adds RL harmfulness rates of 29.9/26.2/21.6% and DPO rates of 49.7/44.6/28.4% for 7B/8B/14B, all above corresponding SFT and SafeKey rates. Table 3 adds distribution-comparison measurements. Section 2.1 replaces the 8B-only 86.7% key-sentence finding with 85.0% for the expanded 8B/14B sample; this is not a same-setting decline.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the reasoning-component definitions, training losses and attention-score definition are unchanged. The added appendices introduce no new theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: identifying a safety aha-moment and using two complementary objectives to improve safety generalization while preserving general abilities. The additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 newly interprets similarity, length and attack-format differences as supporting generalization. Appendix A.4 interprets RL/DPO outcomes as suggesting that conventional alignment methods need adaptation for LRMs. Existing limitations concerning applicability, manual annotation, multi-turn attacks and over-refusal remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The added appendices specify the all-mpnet-base-v2 encoder, space-separated prompt-length calculation, GPT-4o-based RL rewards and DPO negative-response generators: R1-1.5B for unsafe queries and R1-14B for safe queries. Existing SafeKey implementation details, prompt templates and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the bibliography are unchanged. Appendix A.4 adds limited comparative positioning by arguing that conventional RL/DPO alignment may require LRM-specific tuning and adaptation, alongside the demonstrated effectiveness of SafeKey.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to Section 2.1, two new appendix subsections, supporting cross-references, a setup heading, and affiliation/contact information. The main narrative remains stable. The new appendix prose includes unrevised reviewer-response language about incorporating results into a future revision.

P2.justification: v2 adds appendix Tables 3 and 4 for distribution analysis and RL/DPO comparisons. Earlier appendix Tables 3–7 become Tables 5–9, preserving their examples and prompts. Main tables and all seven figures retain their designs, with limited page and column reflow.

improvement.justification: The added RL/DPO comparisons address v1's limited range of alignment baselines, while the distribution analysis and 14B reasoning check provide useful support for existing claims. These gains are limited by sparse baseline-tuning information and absent uncertainty estimates; the new summaries do not fully establish their broader interpretations. Unedited reviewer-response wording slightly weakens presentation, but the net effect is a modest improvement in empirical support.
